text: Grip decreasing. Danger passing, doctors believe.
Philadelphia, nineteen eighteen. The flu, said the paper, had reached its crest. So why was the worst still coming?
A week later: the disease had reached its peak.
Then: high tide. It will begin to recede.
October twelfth. City death toll trebled by grip. Three thousand, two hundred and thirty four deaths in a week.
The government's table: the deadliest week came after that. Four thousand, two hundred and eighteen.
They counted new cases. The deaths came a week later. Danger passing? Not for almost three weeks.
